"Create a 3D action hunting game inspired by Monster Hunter, with weapon combos, large monsters, and simple controls that work well on mobile.

CORE LOOP:
- Choose a weapon, accept a hunt quest, fight a large monster in an arena, and return with rewards
- Win by defeating the monster; lose if health reaches zero or the 10-minute timer runs out
- After each hunt, earn materials used to upgrade weapons

CONTROLS (simple, touch-first):
- Left: virtual joystick for movement
- Right: 4 large buttons: Attack, Special/Heavy Attack, Dodge Roll, Use Item
- Drag the right side of the screen to rotate the camera
- Lock-on button that focuses the camera on the monster
- Auto-targeting assist so attacks lean toward the monster
- Also support keyboard + mouse (WASD, left click, right click, Space to dodge)

WEAPONS (3 types, each with a distinct feel):
1. Great Sword: slow, heavy hits; hold Attack to charge for a powerful strike; can block
2. Dual Blades: fast hits; Special activates a demon mode with a stamina drain and a flurry combo
3. Sword @COMMENT_BODY@ Shield: balanced; can block and use items without sheathing
- Each weapon has a simple 3-hit combo chain (Attack, Attack, Attack) and a unique finisher using Special
- Combos flow by tapping at the right rhythm, with satisfying hit-stop, screen shake, and slash trails
- Weapon models visible in 3D, with different damage numbers, speed, and range per weapon

COMBAT SYSTEM:
- Stamina bar used by dodging, sprinting, and special moves, with fast regeneration
- Dodge roll with brief invincibility frames
- Part-based damage: hitting the head, tail, or wings deals different damage; breaking a part gives bonus rewards
- Damage numbers popping up on hit, and a monster flinch/stagger when hit hard
- Healing potions (limited supply) with a short drinking animation

MONSTERS (3 monsters, each with a unique pattern):
1. Forest Drake: charges, tail sweep, claw swipe, and a roar that briefly stuns
2. Fire Wyvern: fire breath cone, fireball, and aerial dive attacks
3. Ice Behemoth: ground slams, ice shards, and a freezing area attack
- Monster AI with phases: normal, enraged (faster, glowing eyes below 50% HP), and tired (slows down, drools, and flees to rest below 20% HP)
- Clear attack telegraphs (wind-up animations and red ground warnings) so players can learn and dodge
- Monster health bar at the top, with a visible limp and part damage as health drops
- Dramatic intro roar and death animation

ARENA @COMMENT_BODY@ ENVIRONMENT:
- 3 open arenas (forest, volcano, frozen cave) with rocks, trees, and small hills
- Day/night lighting, fog, wind-blown grass, and weather effects like falling ash or snow
- Collision so the player and monster cannot pass through obstacles

PROGRESSION:
- Quest board with 3 hunts of increasing difficulty
- Blacksmith menu: spend monster materials to upgrade weapon damage and unlock new weapon skins
- Save progress automatically

HUD @COMMENT_BODY@ UI:
- Player health and stamina bars, monster health bar, item slot, and quest timer
- Clean minimal menu: Start, Quest Board, Blacksmith, Settings (volume, camera sensitivity, left-handed mode)
- Victory screen showing a reward summary

AUDIO:
- Epic orchestral battle music that builds in intensity when the monster enrages
- Calm ambient music in the hub
- Sound effects for each weapon swing, hit impact, monster roar, and dodge

VISUAL STYLE:
- Stylized low-poly 3D with bold colors, readable silhouettes, and smooth animation
- Prioritize performance on mobile (aim for 60 FPS) with low-poly models and simple particle effects

DEVELOPMENT ORDER:
Start with a playable core: player movement, camera, one weapon with a 3-hit combo, dodge, and one monster with 3 attacks. Then add the other weapons, remaining monsters, arenas, progression, and polish.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the saved project and publish readiness only after both HTTP checks pass.
set -euo pipefail
cd "${PROJECT_DIR:?}"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?}" "${APP_URL:?}"
PORT="${APP_PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
startup_timeout="${STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-600}"
[[ "$startup_timeout" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/time -p test -f start.sh
/usr/bin/time -p bash -n start.sh
current_commit="${CHECKPOINT_COMMIT:-}"
previous_commit=""
[[ ! -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit" ]] || previous_commit="$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit")"
# Reuse an in-flight build for this checkpoint when a readiness retry returns.
starting=false
if [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit" ]] && [[ "$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit")" == "$current_commit" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null; then
  starting=true
fi
if [[ "${RESTART_APP:-false}" == true ]] || { [[ "$starting" == false ]] && { [[ -n "$current_commit" && "$previous_commit" != "$current_commit" ]] || ! /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; }; }; then
  /usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
  /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/reclaim-preview-port.mjs"
  /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
  # Pass paths through tmux's environment; keep the script in the foreground.
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux new-session -d -s app-server -c "$PROJECT_DIR" \
    -e "RUNTIME_DIR=${RUNTIME_DIR:?}" -e "OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" -e "PORT=$PORT" -e "STARTUP_LOG=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.log" \
    'bash start.sh > "$STARTUP_LOG" 2>&1'
fi
ready=false
for ((attempt=0; attempt<(startup_timeout + 1) / 2; attempt++)); do
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
[[ "$ready" == true ]] || { echo "Local startup failed after ${startup_timeout}s. Inspect app.log." >&2; exit 75; }
/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit"
for ((attempt=0; attempt<12; attempt++)); do
  status="$(/usr/bin/time -p curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 --output "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/public-readiness.log" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$APP_URL")" || status=000
  if [[ "$status" == 2* ]]; then
    /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$APP_URL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
    if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT:-}" ]]; then
      /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat" >/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo 'Local and public preview are ready.'
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then
    echo "Public preview rejected the request (HTTP $status). Inspect public-readiness.log." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
echo 'Public preview did not become ready.' >&2
exit 75

Design plan in detail.

### Visuals
Low-poly stylized:
- Player: capsule-ish body from cylinders/boxes, weapon in hand (great sword = big box blade; dual blades = two short blades; sword & shield = blade + shield).
- Monsters: built from primitives with legs, body, head, tail, wings; different color palettes and shapes.
- Arenas: ground plane with vertex colors/noise, rocks (icosahedrons), trees (cones + cylinders), hills. Fog, hemisphere+directional light. Particles: ash/snow, grass blades (instanced simple planes) with wind shader-free animation via per-frame rotation? Use InstancedMesh with shader modification? Simpler: instanced grass strips updated in shader via onBeforeCompile with time. Or just animate a few hundred small planes grouped and rotate whole groups slightly. For perf mobile: use InstancedMesh and update matrices only for a subset each frame? Simpler: grass as InstancedMesh with custom shader patch for wind (sin(time + instance pos)). That's fine.

- Sky: gradient via large sphere shader or scene background color + fog. Use a ShaderMaterial sky dome with day/night colors.

### Game structure
States: BOOT, MENU (title), QUEST_BOARD, BLACKSMITH, SETTINGS, HUNT, RESULT.

Menus are HTML overlays, minimalist. Start → main menu (hub) with Hunt/Quest Board etc. Requirement: "Choose a weapon, accept a hunt quest, fight ... return with rewards". Main menu: Start Hunt (with weapon selector), Quest Board, Blacksmith, Settings.

I'll do:
- Title screen with Start button.
- Hub screen: "Quest Board" (3 quests), "Blacksmith", "Settings", "Equip Weapon" selector visible in quest board.
- Quest card shows monster, arena, difficulty, rewards.
- On hunt start: fade to arena, intro roar cinematic ~2s, timer 10 min.
- HUD with player HP/stamina, monster HP top, timer, item count, lock-on button, combo indicator, weapon name.
- Win/lose screens with rewards.

### Combat
Player state machine:
- idle/move/attack chain/dodge/block/charge/item/dead
- 3-hit combo with chain window. Attack button taps advance chain; if pressed during window, queues next.
- Each weapon has attack data: windup, active, recovery, damage, range, arc, motion value, part multiplier.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-friendly 3D hunting game inspired by Monster Hunter in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Core hunt loop: choose a weapon and quest, fight in an arena, win by defeating the monster, and return with rewards; lose on zero health or a 10-minute timeout.

## IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.

A self-contained, low-poly monster hunting game for desktop and mobile. Pick a weapon, take a quest from the board, break monster parts for extra materials, defeat the beast, and forge stronger gear at the hub.

- **Three weapons:** Great Sword (charge/guard), Dual Blades (Demon Mode), Sword & Shield (guard/bashes)
- **Three hunts:** Forest Drake, Fire Wyvern, Ice Behemoth — each with its own arena, attack patterns, and materials
- **Progression:** weapon upgrades, unlockable skins, auto-saving hunter rank rewards
- **No build step:** all rendering, audio, and models are procedural

### Run locally

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# open http://localhost:3002
```

### Controls

| Action | Keyboard / mouse | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | `WASD` / arrows | Left joystick |
| Attack / charge | `J` or left click (hold to charge Great Sword) | ATTACK |
| Special / guard | `K` or right click | SPECIAL |
| Dodge | `Space` | DODGE |
| Potion | `E` | ITEM |
| Lock on | `F` / `Q` / `Tab` | Target button |
| Camera | Mouse / drag | Drag anywhere |
| Pause | `Esc` | Pause button |

Hunts last up to 10 minutes. Break the head, tail, and wings for bonus materials. Progress saves automatically in the browser.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

- Calm ambient music in the hub

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable mobile-friendly 3D monster-hunting game in the existing project, with hunts, combat, and progression.

## Requirements
- Core loop: choose a weapon and quest, hunt in an arena, win by defeating the monster, and return with upgrade materials; lose at zero health or after 10 minutes.
- Touch-first controls: virtual joystick, four combat/item buttons, camera drag, lock-on, and auto-targeting; also support keyboard and mouse.
- Three distinct weapons with combos and finishers; stamina, dodge invulnerability, part damage, healing, telegraphed monster attacks, and three distinct monsters.
- Three arenas, progression and upgrades, auto-save, minimal menus/HUD, audio, and stylized low-poly visuals optimized for mobile.
- For visual checks, save small JPEGs at no more than 1280px wide and inspect only the latest one.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game titled “IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.” with procedural models, effects, and audio.
- Weapon types are Great Sword, Dual Blades, and Sword & Shield.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game entry, rendering, arenas, player and monster behavior, input, menus/HUD, save/progression, combat effects, and procedural audio.
- Fixed startup issues, including missing `src/main.js` and an `FX.dispose` error; added a visible startup failure screen.
- Added mobile touch-mode layout/controls, updated weapon HUD labeling, softened particle sprites, and fixed Escape-to-resume.
- Verified syntax and browser flows for title, hub, hunts, combat damage, victory/rewards, smith, weapon switching, settings, mobile controls, pause/resume, and timeout.

21: ## IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.
22: 
23: A self-contained, low-poly monster hunting game for desktop and mobile. Pick a weapon, take a quest from the board, break monster parts for extra materials, defeat the beast, and forge stronger gear at the hub.
24: 
25: - **Three weapons:** Great Sword (charge/guard), Dual Blades (Demon Mode), Sword & Shield (guard/bashes)
26: - **Three hunts:** Forest Drake, Fire Wyvern, Ice Behemoth — each with its own arena, attack patterns, and materials
27: - **Progression:** weapon upgrades, unlockable skins, auto-saving rewards
28: - **No build step:** all rendering, audio, and models are procedural
29: 
30: ### Run locally
31: 
32: ```bash
33: python3 -m http.server 3002
34: # open http://localhost:3002
35: ```
36: 
37: ### Controls
38: 
39: | Action | Keyboard / mouse | Touch |
40: | --- | --- | --- |
41: | Move | `WASD` / arrows | Left joystick |
42: | Attack / charge | `J` or left click (hold to charge Great Sword) | ATTACK |
43: | Special / guard | `K` or right click | SPECIAL |
44: | Dodge | `Space` | DODGE |
45: | Potion | `E` | ITEM |
46: | Lock on | `F` / `Q` / `Tab` | Target button |
47: | Camera | Mouse / drag | Drag anywhere |
48: | Pause | `Esc` | Pause button |
49: 
50: Hunts last up to 10 minutes. Break the head, tail, and wings for bonus materials. Progress saves automatically in the browser.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and verify the existing mobile-friendly 3D monster-hunting game with a playable hunt loop and polished mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Support touch-first and keyboard/mouse controls, three weapons and monsters, arenas, progression, audio, and mobile-optimized low-poly visuals.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest one.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game titled “IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.”
- Weapons are Great Sword, Dual Blades, and Sword & Shield.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game loop, combat, monsters, arenas, touch and keyboard/mouse input, menus, HUD, progression, autosave, effects, and audio.
- Added local run instructions and controls to `README.md`.
- Verified all `src/*.js` files parse with `node --check`.
- Browser checks reached the mobile title, hub, quest board, and active hunt; browser reported zero errors and four warnings.
- Previously saved and inspected `screenshots/final-mobile-hunt.jpg` at 360×732 CSS pixels.
- Reparented touch controls out of `#ui` to a direct child of `#app` to address canvas interception; this latest change is not yet browser-verified.

### Active
- Verify touch controls now receive actual pointer events; test lock-on, attack, and other action controls.
- Recheck camera framing in a settled hunt and save/inspect a fresh compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the mobile hunt and verify pointer interaction with the reparented controls, including lock-on and attack.
2. Confirm the monster stays in frame after the intro/camera settles; adjust framing if needed.
3. Rerun browser and syntax checks, save a fresh JPEG no wider than 1280px, and inspect only that newest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Canvas, UI, and touch controls; latest change reparents touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Canvas/UI stacking and mobile control pointer-event rules.
- `src/input.js`: Touch, keyboard, mouse, joystick, and lock-on handlers.
- `src/game.js`: Hunt lifecycle and camera framing/lock-on.
- `src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, and touch visibility.
- `screenshots/final-mobile-hunt.jpg`: Previously inspected mobile hunt screenshot.
- `README.md`: Local run instructions and controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed modified `README.md` and multiple untracked project files/directories.
- Port `3002` already had a server listening; a second server attempt failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.
- Before reparenting, browser clicks reported `#scene` intercepting `#touch-lock` despite `document.elementFromPoint()` resolving to its SVG.
- A later camera projection after the hunt camera settled put the monster near screen center (`NDC x ≈ -0.011`); earlier off-screen readings were captured during camera settling.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the existing mobile-friendly 3D monster-hunting game with a playable hunt loop and polished mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Support touch-first and keyboard/mouse controls, three weapons and monsters, arenas, progression, audio, and mobile-optimized low-poly visuals.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest one.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game titled “IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.”
- Weapons are Great Sword, Dual Blades, and Sword & Shield.
- Reparented touch controls to be a direct child of `#app` to address canvas interception; browser evidence shows they still do not receive real pointer events.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game loop, combat, monsters, arenas, touch and keyboard/mouse input, menus, HUD, progression, autosave, effects, and audio.
- Added local run instructions and controls to `README.md`.
- Verified all `src/*.js` files parse with `node --check`.
- Browser checks reached the mobile title, hub, quest board, and active hunt; browser reported zero errors and four warnings.
- Verified `toggleLock()` works in code, and touch lock pointerdown increments the queued lock press.

### Active
- Fix touch-control hit testing and verify actual lock-on, attack, and other action input.
- Recheck camera framing in a settled hunt, then save and inspect a fresh compliant JPEG screenshot.
- Rerun browser and syntax checks after changes.

### Blocked
- Real pointer input at touch control coordinates reaches `#scene` rather than `#touch-lock`; this persisted after moving touch controls under `#app`. Browser mouse click timed out with `canvas#scene intercepts pointer events`; raw pointerdown hit `scene`. A synthetic pointer event directly dispatched to the lock button increments `game.input.presses.lock`, but does not demonstrate real interaction.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the live DOM and stacking/hit-test chain around `#app`, `#scene`, `#ui`, and `#touch-controls`; fix the canvas interception.
2. Reload into a hunt and test actual lock-on and attack/action controls via browser pointer input.
3. Check settled camera framing; run syntax/browser checks, capture a new JPEG no wider than 1280px, and inspect only that newest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Canvas, UI, and touch controls; controls were moved out of `#ui` but are still intercepted.
- `styles.css`: Canvas/UI stacking and touch-control pointer-event rules.
- `src/input.js`: Touch, keyboard, mouse, joystick, and lock-on handlers.
- `src/game.js`: Hunt lifecycle, `toggleLock()`, and camera framing/lock-on.
- `src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, and touch visibility.
- `screenshots/final-mobile-hunt.jpg`: Previously inspected mobile hunt screenshot; replace with a fresh verification capture.
- `README.md`: Local run instructions and controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` previously showed modified `README.md` and multiple untracked project files/directories.
- Port `3002` has an existing server; an additional server attempt failed with `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.
- The mobile browser viewport is 360×732 CSS pixels at DPR 3.
- Settled camera projection previously put the monster near screen center (`NDC x ≈ -0.011`); earlier off-screen readings were captured during camera settling.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the mobile-friendly 3D monster-hunting game with a playable hunt loop and polished mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Support touch-first and keyboard/mouse controls, three weapons and monsters, arenas, progression, audio, and mobile-optimized low-poly visuals.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px and inspect only the latest one.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game titled “IRONFANG — Hunt. Break. Forge.”
- Weapons are Great Sword, Dual Blades, and Sword & Shield.
- Touch controls sit outside `#ui` under `#app` to address canvas interception.
- The lock button marks touch input; UI click toggles lock-on. Keyboard lock presses are consumed during hunt updates.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game loop, combat, monsters, arenas, touch and keyboard/mouse input, menus, HUD, progression, autosave, effects, and audio.
- Added local run instructions and controls to `README.md`.
- Touchscreen-emulated tap on `#touch-lock` successfully toggles `game.lockOn`; touch input is marked used.
- Touch joystick movement works and reduced the player-to-monster distance.
- After moving into attack range, touchscreen-emulated attack reduced monster health from 780 to 662.02 and recorded 102 damage.

### Active
- Rerun browser and syntax checks, verify settled hunt camera framing, and capture/inspect a fresh compliant JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- Browser CLI mouse clicks target `scene` rather than touch controls; use touchscreen-emulated taps for touch verification.

## Next Move
1. Check settled hunt camera framing and any remaining touch actions.
2. Run browser and syntax checks.
3. Capture a fresh JPEG no wider than 1280px and inspect only that newest screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Canvas, UI, and touch controls.
- `styles.css`: Canvas/UI stacking and touch-control hit areas.
- `src/input.js`: Touch, keyboard, mouse, joystick, and lock-on input handlers.
- `src/player.js`: Player attacks and combat state machine.
- `src/game.js`: Hunt lifecycle, combat updates, lock-on, and camera framing.
- `src/ui.js`: Menus, HUD, and touch-control visibility.
- `screenshots/final-mobile-hunt.jpg`: Older inspected screenshot; replace with a fresh verification capture.
- `README.md`: Local run instructions and controls.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed modified `README.md` and untracked `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, `index.html`, `src/`, `styles.css`, and `vendor/`.
- The earlier zero-damage attack was a range issue: the player was about 5.6 units from the monster while the Great Sword attack reach is 3.25; closing in with the joystick allowed damage to register.
